questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Honestly, it's not very easy. You get a lot of emails, most of them are not useful, but there are some really important ones mixed in, so make sure to read them all. I’d recommend sorting out as much as you can before you go—it makes the arrival so much less confusing

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There’s a welcome week where they cover the most essential information, and you can get help if needed. Don’t hesitate to reach out to the school administration—they are very helpful. I contacted them multiple times, and they guided me or directed me to the right staff when necessary

questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: When i prepared to go, i got the assumption that it was easy to find accomodation outside campus. But it is not, so sort the out housing situation early. I found my housing through Airbnp( not cheap)

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I stayed in Hamilton downtown for the first couple of weeks, but I wouldn’t recommend staying there—there are many crackheads and shady people. I’d suggest staying in Westdale or as close to campus as possible. If you already have friends to live with, that’s great, but if you’re going alone, I’d recommend staying on campus. There will be loads of exchange students there, making it much easier to socialize

questions.answer: It’s pretty straightforward. Once you get your McMaster account, you can simply pick and choose the courses you like. There’s a cool feature that lets you create your schedule before actually registering for a course. This way, you can plan your timetable to match your preferred school hours

questions.answer: I used the gym, pool, squash, table tennis, badminton and more. The best part is that it is free for all undergrad students

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I highly recommend to check out McMaster outdoor club. I participated in a camping trip in algonquin and i can honestly say that is was my hightlight of the whole exchange. It cost about 300 bucks, but you get everything you need. And explore the nature it is by far the best to do in canada

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Most of the students my year was a bit young to be fair. They start school before us, so it was easier to befriend other exchange students
